vocabulary.meaning_en: to decide which tasks are most important and do them first
vocabulary.meaning_ar: يرتّب الأولويات؛ يقدّم الأهم على المهم
vocabulary.note_en: UK spelling: prioritise; US spelling: prioritize.
vocabulary.example: I have three reports to write, so I need to prioritise.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something that is more important than other things
vocabulary.example: Finishing the contract is my top priority this week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give all your attention to one thing
vocabulary.example: Please let me concentrate on this report for an hour.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a piece of work that you have to do
vocabulary.example: Answering customer emails is my first task every morning.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give part of your work to another person
vocabulary.example: A good manager knows how to delegate work to the team.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to move something to a later time
vocabulary.example: We put off the meeting until Monday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a list that shows who does a job and when
vocabulary.note_ar: كلمة بريطانية؛ في الأمريكية schedule أو roster.
vocabulary.note_en: British English; Americans often say schedule or roster.
vocabulary.example: The cleaning rota is on the kitchen wall.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to prepare and write a plan, list or document
vocabulary.example: Could you draw up a list of our suppliers?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a job or duty that you must do
vocabulary.example: Ordering paper is Denise's responsibility.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to do something one after another, not all at the same time
vocabulary.example: We take it in turns to make coffee for the team.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to have or do something together with other people
vocabulary.example: Let's share the work so nobody is too busy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give someone their old job back
vocabulary.example: After the mistake was found, the company reinstated her.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to try doing something
vocabulary.example: I'd like to have a go at writing the newsletter.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to begin doing a piece of work
vocabulary.example: Could you make a start on the sales report today?

vocabulary.meaning_en: feeling worried because you have too much to do
vocabulary.example: Everyone is under pressure before the deadline.

vocabulary.meaning_en: worried and tense because of work or problems
vocabulary.example: He feels stressed when he has too many emails.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to plan your work and things so you can work well
vocabulary.example: I wrote a to-do list to get organised.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a list of jobs you need to do
vocabulary.example: The first item on my to-do list is calling the client.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a written business agreement
vocabulary.example: We signed a new contract with the supplier.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the event when a new product is first shown or sold
vocabulary.example: The product launch is on Friday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: between two people who disagree, and not able to please both
vocabulary.example: When my two colleagues argue, I'm caught in the middle.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a way to solve a problem
vocabulary.example: Sharing the work is a good solution.

fine_lines.title: prioritise vs priority
fine_lines.explanation_ar: prioritise فعل معناه «يرتّب الأولويات»، أما priority فهو اسم معناه «أولوية». بعد الفعل نضع عادةً مفعولًا أو لا شيء، وقبل الاسم نستخدم كلمات مثل my أو top.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Prioritise is a verb (an action). Priority is a noun (a thing). We say 'I need to prioritise' but 'This is my top priority'.

examples.sentence: When you are busy, you must prioritise.
Customer safety is our first priority.

fine_lines.title: put off vs call off
fine_lines.explanation_ar: put off يعني تأجيل الأمر إلى وقت لاحق، فهو سيحدث لاحقًا. أما call off فيعني إلغاء الأمر نهائيًّا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Put off means move to a later time; it will still happen. Call off means cancel; it will not happen.

examples.sentence: We put off the meeting until next week.
They called off the meeting because the client cancelled.

expressions.phrase: I've got to prioritise. This task is the most important so I'm going to concentrate on this first.
expressions.meaning_ar: يجب أن أرتّب أولوياتي. هذه المهمة هي الأهم، لذلك سأركّز عليها أولًا.
expressions.meaning_en: I must decide what is most important; I will do this task first.
expressions.example: I've got to prioritise. The client report is the most important, so I'm going to concentrate on it first.

expressions.phrase: It would be a great help if you could do this for me, please.
expressions.meaning_ar: سيكون عونًا كبيرًا لو استطعت أن تقوم بهذا عني من فضلك.
expressions.meaning_en: A very polite way to ask someone to do a task for you.
expressions.example: It would be a great help if you could answer the phone this morning.

expressions.phrase: I'm going to have to put that off until tomorrow, I'm afraid.
expressions.meaning_ar: للأسف سأضطر إلى تأجيل ذلك إلى الغد.
expressions.meaning_en: I can't do that now; I will do it tomorrow (said politely).
expressions.example: I'm going to have to put the training off until tomorrow, I'm afraid.

expressions.phrase: I need help. I have too much to do.
expressions.meaning_ar: أحتاج إلى مساعدة؛ لديّ عمل كثير جدًّا.
expressions.meaning_en: Tell your manager you have too much work.
expressions.example: Sorry to bother you, but I have too much to do and I need some help.

expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to start talking to a busy person.
expressions.example: Sorry to bother you, but do you have a minute?

expressions.phrase: Could I suggest we all take it in turns?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل لي أن أقترح أن نتناوب جميعًا؟
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to suggest sharing a job.
expressions.example: Could I suggest we all take it in turns to lock the office?

expressions.meaning_en: I understand what you mean (even if I don't fully agree).
expressions.example: I see your point, but we still need someone to order the paper.

expressions.meaning_en: Let's make sure we understand the situation clearly.
expressions.example: Let's get this straight: you want to work in sales now?

grammar.title: Polite requests: It would be a great help if you could…
grammar.explanation_ar: لطلب شيء بأدب شديد نستخدم: It would be a great help if you could + الفعل في المصدر. الكلمتان would وcould تجعلان الطلب أكثر لطفًا من Do this.
grammar.explanation_en: To ask very politely, use: It would be a great help if you could + base verb. 'Would' and 'could' make the request softer than an order.
examples: It would be a great help if you could check these figures.
It would be a great help if you could call the supplier.
It would be really helpful if you could send me the file.

grammar.title: have got to / be going to have to
grammar.explanation_ar: I've got to = I have to: يجب عليّ (التزام الآن). أما I'm going to have to فتعني «سأضطر إلى» في المستقبل، وغالبًا نستخدمها لإبلاغ خبر غير مرغوب بلطف، مع I'm afraid.
grammar.explanation_en: 'I've got to' means 'I have to' (I must, now). 'I'm going to have to' means I will be forced to do something in the future; we use it with 'I'm afraid' for news people won't like.
examples: I've got to finish this report today.
We're going to have to cancel the trip, I'm afraid.
She's going to have to work late tonight.

questions.question: What does 'prioritise' mean?
choices: decide which tasks are most important
finish all tasks at the same time
give your job to someone else
questions.explanation_ar: prioritise يعني أن تقرر أيّ المهام أهم وتبدأ بها.
questions.explanation_en: To prioritise is to decide what is most important and do it first.

questions.question: I'm going to have to ___ that ___ until tomorrow, I'm afraid.
questions.explanation_en: 'Put off' means move to a later time.

questions.question: Which request is the most polite?
choices: It would be a great help if you could do this for me.
questions.explanation_ar: استخدام would وcould يجعل الطلب مهذبًا جدًّا.
questions.explanation_en: 'It would be a great help if you could...' is very polite.

questions.question: Anna asks Denise to make a list of who orders pens and when. What is this list called?
questions.explanation_ar: rota قائمة تبيّن من يقوم بالعمل ومتى.
questions.explanation_en: A rota shows who does a job and when.

questions.question: 'Delegate' means…
choices: give part of your work to someone else
questions.explanation_ar: delegate يعني تفويض جزء من عملك لشخص آخر.
questions.explanation_en: To delegate is to give some of your work to another person.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation_ar: priority اسم، ونقول my top priority.

questions.question: The meeting is not cancelled; it is just moved to next week. We ___ the meeting.
questions.explanation_ar: put off تأجيل، أما call off فإلغاء.
questions.explanation_en: Put off = move later; call off = cancel.

questions.question: 'We take it in turns to order the paper' means…
choices: each person orders it one after another
questions.explanation_ar: take it in turns يعني أن كل شخص يقوم بالأمر في دوره.
questions.explanation_en: Take it in turns means one person, then the next person, and so on.

questions.question: I've got to finish this today. 'I've got to' means…
questions.explanation_ar: I've got to تعني I have to أي يجب عليّ.

questions.question: Which is a polite way to start talking to a busy colleague?
questions.explanation_ar: Sorry to bother you عبارة مهذبة لبدء الحديث مع شخص مشغول.
questions.explanation_en: 'Sorry to bother you, but...' is a polite opener.
